blueprint.primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
blueprint.content_focus: TAP2-dependent MHC class I peptide loading

item.vignette: A 9-year-old boy has recurrent bacterial respiratory infections and bronchiectasis. Flow cytometry shows markedly reduced HLA class I expression on nucleated cells, preserved HLA class II expression, and a low CD8+ T-cell count with a normal CD4+ T-cell count. Genetic testing identifies biallelic loss-of-function variants in TAP2.
item.lead_in: Which intracellular step is most directly impaired by this defect?

options.A: Proteasomal cleavage of cytosolic proteins into peptide fragments
options.B: Removal of invariant-chain-derived peptide from MHC class II molecules in acidified endosomes
options.C: Transport of newly synthesized MHC class II molecules from the endoplasmic reticulum to endosomal compartments
options.D: ATP-dependent transport of cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum for loading onto MHC class I molecules
options.E: Endocytosis of extracellular proteins for presentation to CD4+ T cells

item.difficulty_basis: Expert estimate only; requires linking TAP2 loss and low MHC I/CD8 cells to the peptide-translocation step of endogenous antigen presentation.
item.tested_construct: TAP1/TAP2 transport cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading

explanation.key_explanation: TAP is a heterodimer composed of TAP1 and TAP2 that uses ATP to move cytosolic peptides into the endoplasmic reticulum. These peptides are loaded onto nascent MHC class I molecules before surface expression. TAP2 loss therefore reduces peptide-loaded MHC class I at the cell surface and is associated with selective CD8+ T-cell lymphopenia.

distractor_explanations.A: The proteasome generates many cytosolic peptides upstream of TAP; TAP2 transports those peptides rather than cleaving proteins.
distractor_explanations.B: Removal of CLIP from MHC class II is mediated by HLA-DM in endosomal compartments and belongs to the exogenous antigen-presentation pathway.
distractor_explanations.C: MHC class II trafficking to endosomes depends on the invariant-chain pathway, not TAP2.
distractor_explanations.D: Correct. TAP1/TAP2 translocate cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading.
distractor_explanations.E: Endocytosis of extracellular antigen primarily supports MHC class II presentation to CD4+ T cells and does not explain the selective MHC class I defect.

explanation.educational_objective: TAP1/TAP2 use ATP to transport cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading; TAP deficiency lowers surface MHC I and can produce selective CD8+ T-cell lymphopenia.

evidence_map.claim: TAP1/TAP2 form an ATP-dependent transporter that moves cytosolic peptides into the ER for MHC class I loading.
TAP2-associated MHC class I deficiency is associated with selective CD8+ T-cell lymphopenia and recurrent respiratory disease.
